As the frameworks used to understand nuclear strategy become outdated, a re-evaluation of defense policy and missile defense is urgently needed to adapt to these realities.

 - Future nuclear deterrence strategies must account for the realities of heightened civilian casualties in any military engagement against the U.S.

Recent research has determined the computational difficulty of achieving equilibria in Bertrand networks, a type of game theory model where sellers set prices without discrimination across markets. The findings indicate that calculating any approximate Nash equilibrium is a complex task classified as PPAD-complete, presenting challenges even in relatively simple graph structures. Additionally, the research establishes that every achievable equilibrium revenue profile can be represented with a structural complexity that is finite but may require significant computational resources for exact solutions.

 - The research identifies the computational intractability of finding approximate Nash equilibria in Bertrand networks.
 - It shows that an exact equilibrium can be achieved with finite complexity, although it may require significant computational effort.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22216
